_comment: The entire 'web' this tutorial's search tool can see. Ten short pages about the fictional town of Willow Creek. Deliberately fictional: none of these facts exist anywhere else, so if the model speaks one of them, it read this file — it cannot have known it. Edit a fact, reload, ask again; the answer must change. One file, so you can read or edit the whole thing without touching code.

pages.title: Willow Creek ferry moves to its winter schedule
pages.snippet: From Monday the ferry leaves on the quarter hour, with the last crossing at 9:45 pm.

pages.title: Night market returns to Harbor Street
pages.snippet: The Friday night market is back this week, running 5 pm to 10 pm through the end of the month.

pages.title: Sourdough prize goes to Harbor Street bakery
pages.snippet: Miller & Finch took the national sourdough prize with a rye loaf fermented for 60 hours.

pages.title: Willow Creek weekend forecast
pages.snippet: Saturday brings light rain and a high of 16 degrees; Sunday clears, with a high of 19.

pages.title: Otters take the regional final
pages.snippet: The Willow Creek Otters beat Eastport 3 to 2 on a stoppage-time goal by Ada Okafor.

pages.title: Marathon route changes announced
pages.snippet: This year's Willow Creek marathon skips the causeway; the course now climbs Beacon Hill twice.

pages.title: Comet Verlaine visible this month
pages.snippet: Comet Verlaine sits low in the northeast just before dawn for the rest of the month; no telescope needed.

pages.title: University counts its puffins
pages.snippet: The annual puffin census recorded 8,140 birds on the north cliffs, up six percent from last year.

pages.title: Lighthouse museum extends its hours
pages.snippet: The Museum of Lighthouse Optics now stays open until 7 pm on weekends, and admission is still free.

pages.title: Beacon Hill funicular reopens
pages.snippet: After a two-year restoration the funicular runs daily, every 20 minutes, weather permitting.
